Simplify ((x²−1)/(x²−4))((x−2)/(x−1)) and state the original restrictions.
Factor (x−1)(x+1)/[(x−2)(x+2)] and cancel x−1 and x−2. Keep zeros of both original denominators.
The denominator D(x)=x²−(k+1)x+k has exactly two distinct forbidden inputs, 1 and 3. Find k.
Factor D(x)=(x−1)(x−k). The two zeros are 1 and k; since they are 1 and 3, k=3.

For (x²−16)/(x+4), identify the excluded input and explain whether x=4 is allowed.
Only the denominator x+4 restricts the domain. A zero numerator at x=4 is allowed.
Exclude zeros of internal denominators x−4 and x+2 and the zero of the divisor numerator x+1.
If D(x)=x²−(a+2)x+2a and the expression 1/D(x) is undefined at exactly x=2 and x=5, find a.
Factor D(x)=(x−2)(x−a). The other root must be 5, so a=5.
